'''Dragan Bender''' (born 17 November 1997) is a Croatian former professional [[basketball]] player. He stands {{Convert|7|ft|0|in|m|abbr=on}} and played the [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]] and [[center (basketball)|center]] positions. He was selected by the [[Phoenix Suns]] with the fourth overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]] but only played four years in the league. Bender represents the [[Croatia men's national basketball team|Croatian national team]], with experience in the [[FIBA Europe]] junior tournaments. Before playing in Israel, he competed with multiple teams in Croatia and in [[Nikola Vujčić]]'s academy.

==Early life==
Bender was born on 17 November 1997, in [[Čapljina]], [[Bosnia and Herzegovina]], and he later moved to [[Split, Croatia]].<ref name="NBA Draft">{{cite web|url=http://www.nbadraft.net/players/dragan-bender |title=NBA Draft |website=NBA Draft.net |access-date=4 January 2015}}</ref> At 12 years of age, he started playing at [[Nikola Vujčić]]'s basketball academy as a [[point guard]].<ref name=jpost/> Vujčić was a former [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] star and became Bender's guardian.<ref name="br">{{cite web|last1=Pick|first1=David|title=Meet 17-Year-Old European Dragan Bender, Who Could Be 2016's Kristaps Porzingis|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2573742-meet-17-year-old-european-dragan-bender-who-could-be-2016s-kristaps-porzingis|website=[[Bleacher Report]]|access-date=13 March 2016}}</ref> At the academy, Bender became a more versatile player and he "learned how to play all the positions on the court."<ref name="fastbreak">{{cite web|last1=Wonsover|first1=Michael|title=International Prospects Bender and Gentile Impress in American Tour|url=http://www.todaysfastbreak.com/nba-draft/bender-gentile-impress-american-tour/|website=Today's Fastbreak|access-date=13 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160626102912/http://www.todaysfastbreak.com/nba-draft/bender-gentile-impress-american-tour/|archive-date=26 June 2016}}</ref> Bender played there along with his older brother, Ivan, with Bender also playing against guys that were Ivan's age when he first started playing.<ref name="si">{{cite magazine|last1=Fischer|first1=Jake|title=Croatian Dragan Bender at epicenter of historic Maccabi-Milano rivalry tour|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2015/09/28/dragan-bender-nba-draft-croatia-maccabi-tel-aviv-olimpia-milano-dario-saric|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=28 September 2015 |access-date=13 March 2016}}</ref> Bender also played with the [[KK Split]] youth teams at this time, and he appeared for the Croatian under-16 national basketball team.<ref name="yahoo">{{cite web|last1=Givony|first1=Jonathan|title=European Dispatch: Getting to know Dragan Bender|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/european-dispatch--getting-to-know-dragan-bender-195451386.html|website=[[Yahoo! Sports]]|date=5 February 2016 |access-date=13 March 2016}}</ref> He idolized and modeled his game after [[Toni Kukoč]], a former Croatian [[NBA]] player, while growing up and watched his old game tape.<ref name="jpost">{{cite web|last1=Sinai|first1=Allon|title=Mac TA's Bender braces for added attention in next step en route to NBA|url=https://www.jpost.com/Israel-News/Sports/Sinai-says-Mac-TAs-Bender-braces-for-added-attention-in-next-step-en-route-to-NBA-421125|website=[[The Jerusalem Post]]|date=7 October 2015 |access-date=13 March 2016}}</ref> He mostly watched [[EuroLeague]] games but would sometimes tune into the NBA as well. One of his favorite EuroLeague players was [[Šarūnas Jasikevičius]].<ref name=si/>

==Professional career==

===Split (2012–2013)===
Bender made his professional debut at 15 years of age with [[KK Split]]. He played only a total of six minutes and added two points and one rebound.<ref name=yahoo/><ref name="eurobasket">{{cite web|title=Dragan Bender player profile|url=http://basketball.eurobasket.com/player/Dragan_Bender/Maccabi_Fox_Tel-Aviv/242116|website=[[Eurobasket.com]]|access-date=13 March 2016}}</ref>

=== Kaštela (2013–2014) ===
For the following season, Bender remained in Croatia and signed with [[KK Kaštela]], who played in the country's second-best league.<ref name="euroleague">{{cite web|title=Bender, Dragan|url=http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=004549&seasoncode=JT12#!biography|website=[[Euroleague Basketball]]|access-date=13 March 2016}}</ref> With his help, the team was promoted to the [[A-1 Liga]], the top league in Croatia.<ref name="kastela">{{cite web|title=Bender zakucavanjem odveo Kaštelane na prag A1 lige|url=http://www.kastela.org/kastela/udruge/135-novosti/21402-kosarka-bender-zakucavanjem-odveo-kastelane-na-prag-a1-lige|website=Kastela.org|access-date=13 March 2016|language=hr}}</ref> Most notably, he made a game-winning shot with three seconds remaining against [[KK Gorica]] to help his team secure the promotion.<ref name="kastela" /> Later, in February 2014, Bender joined the [[KK Cedevita]] junior team for the [[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]]. He put up 21 points, 9 rebounds, and 6 assists vs the junior team of the Serbian club [[KK Mega Basket]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Dragan Bender Game Logs|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Dragan-Bender/GameLogs/41582/International/2014|website=[[RealGM]]|access-date=13 March 2016}}</ref>

===Ironi Ramat Gan (2014–2016)===
In 2014, Bender signed a seven-year contract with [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]], a team that played in the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref name="future">{{cite web|last1=O'Donnell|first1=Ricky|title=The future of basketball looks a lot like Croatia's Dragan Bender|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2015/6/8/8745739/dragan-bender-nba-draft-2016-profile|website=[[SB Nation]]|date=8 June 2015|access-date=13 March 2016}}</ref> He was soon [[loan (sports)|loaned]] to [[Ironi Ramat Gan]] of the [[Liga Leumit (basketball)|Liga Leumit]], the second-tier-level league in Israel, for the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=2015 adidas Eurocamp: Day One|url=http://www.draftexpress.com/article/2015-adidas-Eurocamp-Day-One-5059|website=DraftExpress|access-date=13 March 2016}}</ref> He made his debut on 21 October 2014, posting 13 points, 13 rebounds, and 4 assists vs [[A.S. Ramat HaSharon|Ramat HaSharon]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ironi Ramat Gan - Ramat Hasharon 87-83|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/Israel/2014/1021_437_903.asp|website=[[Eurobasket.com]]|access-date=13 March 2016}}</ref> He recorded another [[Double-double (basketball)|double-double]] on 12 December, with 23 points and 12 rebounds in a win over [[Maccabi Ra'anana]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Maccabi Raanana - Ironi Ramat Gan 73-88|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/Israel/2014/1202_10044_437.asp|website=[[Eurobasket.com]]|access-date=13 March 2016}}</ref> Bender scored a season-high 25 points as his team defeated [[Elitzur Netanya B.C.|Barak Netanya]] by one point on 1 January 2015.<ref>{{cite web|title=Netanya - Ironi Ramat Gan 95-96|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/Israel/2015/0101_1630_437.asp|website=[[Eurobasket.com]]|access-date=13 March 2016}}</ref> After 28 games, he finished the season averaging 9.7 points, 7.4 rebounds, 2.6 assists, and 1.1 blocks.<ref name=eurobasket/> As the season came to a close, Bender returned to Maccabi Tel Aviv.<ref>{{cite web|title=Maccabi Tel Aviv out to avenge recent flops as BSL season tips off|url=https://www.jpost.com/Israel-News/Sports/Maccabi-Tel-Aviv-out-to-avenge-recent-flops-as-BSL-season-tips-off-421411|website=[[The Jerusalem Post]]|date=9 October 2015 |access-date=13 March 2016}}</ref>

=== Maccabi Tel Aviv (2015–2016) ===
[[File:Bender BoxOut.JPG|thumb|Bender (#3) with Maccabi Tel Aviv in 2015]]
Bender debuted for Maccabi Tel Aviv in the Israeli Premier League on 11 October 2015, with 5 points, 3 rebounds, and 3 blocks in a win over [[Maccabi Kiryat Gat B.C.|Maccabi Kiryat Gat]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Maccabi T-A - Maccabi K/G 89-65|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/Israel/2015/1011_159_1828.asp|website=[[Eurobasket.com]]|access-date=6 April 2016}}</ref> He scored double figures for the first time with the team in a rematch with Kiryat Gat, adding 15 points.<ref name=yahoo/><ref>{{cite web|title=Maccabi K/G - Maccabi T-A 63-88|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/Israel/2015/1220_1828_159.asp|website=[[Eurobasket.com]]|access-date=6 April 2016}}</ref> Bender scored a season-high 16 points on 31 December 2015, as his team defeated [[Hapoel Holon]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Maccabi T-A - Hapoel Holon 93-75|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/Israel/2015/1231_159_436.asp|website=[[Eurobasket.com]]|access-date=6 April 2016}}</ref> In 2015–16, he helped Maccabi Tel Aviv repeat as winners in the [[2015–16 Israeli Basketball State Cup|2016 Israeli State Cup]], and he was named a foreign All-Star for the 2016 Israeli All-Star game.

On 6 April 2016, Bender declared for the [[2016 NBA draft]].<ref>[http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/241459/Dragan-Bender-Declares-For-NBA-Draft Dragan Bender Declares For NBA Draft]</ref> His contract with Maccabi Tel Aviv was later bought out for $1.3 million.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/news/source--dragan-bender-has--1-3-million-buyout-164937868.html Source: Top prospect Dragan Bender has $1.3 million buyout]</ref>

===Phoenix Suns (2016–2019)===
On 23 June 2016, Bender was selected by the [[Phoenix Suns]] with the fourth overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2016/06/23/dragan-bender-2016-nba-draft|title=Suns select Dragan Bender with No. 4 pick|work=SI.com|date=23 June 2016|access-date=12 July 2016}}</ref> He was widely billed as the best international prospect available in the draft, highly valued for his ability to shoot the ball in various ways as a big man, as well as his overall untapped potential in other facets of the game.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-select-dragan-bender-fourth-pick-2016-nba-draft Suns Select Dragan Bender with 4th Pick of 2016 NBA Draft]</ref> As the fourth overall pick, Bender became the Suns' highest-selected rookie since [[Armen Gilliam]] was taken second overall in [[1987 NBA draft|1987]],<ref>[http://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2016/06/23/phoenix-suns-2016-draft-pick/86262130/ Phoenix Suns take Dragan Bender No. 4 in NBA draft]</ref> and the highest-selected Croatian to be taken in an NBA draft. On 7 July, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Suns and joined the team for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-dragan-bender-marquese-chriss-and-tyler-ulis Suns Sign Dragan Bender, Marquese Chriss and Tyler Ulis]</ref> Bender made his debut for the Suns in their season opener on 26 October 2016, scoring 10 points on 4-of-5 shooting in a 113–94 loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899412|title=Kings vs. Suns – Box Score|work=ESPN.com|date=26 October 2016|access-date=27 October 2016}}</ref> With Bender playing alongside [[Devin Booker]] and fellow rookie [[Marquese Chriss]], the Suns became the first NBA team to get three teenagers on the floor in the same game.<ref>[http://www.brightsideofthesun.com/2016/10/26/13403140/opening-night-game-preview-phoenix-suns-sacramento-kings-tv-radio-what-to-watch Opening Night Game Preview: Phoenix Suns kick off season against Sacramento Kings]</ref> Bender also joined Booker and [[Giannis Antetokounmpo]] as the only 18-year-olds to score 10 points in a game since 2006–07.<ref>[https://twitter.com/SunsBballComm/status/791497440792674305 Bender is first @NBA 18y/o to score 10+ in a...]</ref> He had his second 10-point game of the season on 8 November in a 124–121 loss to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899553 Suns vs. Trail Blazers – Box Score]</ref> He then had his third 10-point game of the season on 3 December in a 138–109 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com.au/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899741 Suns vs. Warriors – Box Score]</ref> On 26 December, Bender recorded his first career double-double with season highs of 11 points and 13 rebounds in a 131–115 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899909 Harden scores 32 points and Rockets cruise past Suns 131-115]</ref> On 8 February 2017, Bender underwent a successful routine arthroscopic procedure on his right ankle to remove a bone spur. He was subsequently ruled out for approximately four to six weeks.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/bender-undergoes-successful-surgery Dragan Bender Undergoes Successful Surgery]</ref> He returned to action on 2 April 2017, against Houston.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899475 Rockets, without Harden, send Suns to 12th straight loss]</ref>

In July 2017, Bender re-joined the Suns for the [[2017 NBA Summer League]].<ref>[http://arizonasports.com/story/1165849/phoenix-suns-announce-roster-nba-summer-league-las-vegas/ Phoenix Suns announce roster for NBA Summer League in Las Vegas]</ref> In five games, he averaged 14.2 points, 6.0 rebounds, and 2.4 assists per game. On 13 November 2017, Bender scored a career-high 15 points in a 100–93 loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974947|title=Clarkson scores 25, Lakers beat Suns 100-93|work=ESPN.com|date=13 November 2017|access-date=13 November 2017}}</ref> On 16 December 2017, he set a new career high with 17 points in a 108–106 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/suns-dragan-bender-scores-career-high-17-points-saturday/|title=Suns' Dragan Bender: Scores career-high 17 points Saturday|work=cbssports.com|date=17 December 2017|access-date=27 December 2017}}</ref> On 7 January 2018, he scored 17 of his then career-high 20 points in the second half of the Suns' 114–100 win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. He made a career-best six 3-pointers, going 5 of 6 in the second half.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975334|title=Reserves Bender, Jackson help Suns beat Thunder 114-100|work=ESPN.com|date=7 January 2018|access-date=7 January 2018}}</ref> On 10 February 2018, he scored a career-high 23 points in a 123–113 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975578|title=Nuggets use big second-half run to beat Suns 123-113|work=ESPN.com|date=10 February 2018|access-date=11 February 2018}}</ref> On 8 April 2018, Bender recorded 14 points and a career-high 14 rebounds in a 117–100 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975949|title=Thompson, Warriors beat Suns for 15th straight time|work=ESPN.com|date=8 April 2018|access-date=30 October 2018}}</ref>

In July 2018, Bender re-joined the Suns for the [[2018 NBA Summer League]].<ref>[https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-announce-2018-summer-league-roster Suns Announce 2018 Summer League Roster]</ref> On 30 October 2018, the Suns declined Bender's $5.9 million fourth year rookie option, making him a free agent after the season. On 5 April 2019, Bender recorded a career-high seven blocks in a 133–126 overtime win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071862|title=Jackson nets 35 points, Suns beat Pelicans in overtime|work=ESPN.com|date=5 April 2019|access-date=10 April 2019}}</ref>

===Milwaukee Bucks (2019–2020)===
In July 2019, Bender signed a two-year minimum deal with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/bucks-sign-dragan-bender|title=Bucks Sign Dragan Bender|website=NBA.com|date=30 July 2019|access-date=6 August 2019}}</ref> The first year of Bender's deal was partially guaranteed, but it became fully guaranteed when the Bucks did not waive Bender by 7 January, while the second is non-guaranteed.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/nba/bucks/2019/07/25/bucks-sign-dragan-bender-21-two-year-contract/1826505001/|title=Bucks sign dragan bender 21 two year contract|work=jsonline.com|date=25 July 2019|access-date=25 July 2019}}</ref> Bender was assigned to the [[Wisconsin Herd]] for the start of the [[NBA G League]] season. On 10 February 2020, the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] announced that they had waived Bender.<ref>{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Request Waivers On Dragan Bender|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-request-waivers-dragan-bender|date=10 February 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=10 February 2020}}</ref>

===Golden State Warriors (2020)===
On 23 February 2020, the [[Golden State Warriors]] announced that they had signed Bender to a 10-day contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Warriors Sign Center Dragan Bender to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-dragan-bender-20200223|date=23 February 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=23 February 2020}}</ref> In his first game he played against his former team, the [[Phoenix Suns]], he recorded 13 points and 9 rebounds in a 115–99 win on 29 February.<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202002290PHO.html| title = Golden State Warriors at Phoenix Suns Box Score, February 29, 2020 {{!}} Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref> He then acquired a second 10-day contract on 5 March 2020. In his last game before the [[Suspension of the 2019–20 NBA season|NBA season was suspended]] due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]], Bender tied his career high with 23 points on 8-of-12 shooting and added 7 rebounds in a 131–107 loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] on 10 March.<ref>{{cite web|title=Warriors Sign Center Dragan Bender to Second 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-dragan-bender-20200305|date=5 March 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=5 March 2020}}</ref> The season was suspended while Bender was still on contract, and he became a free agent before the season restarted in July.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Joakim Noah to sign deal with Clippers for rest of season|url=https://www.yardbarker.com/nba/articles/report_joakim_noah_to_sign_deal_with_clippers_for_rest_of_season/s1_13132_32224220|date=20 June 2020|website=yardbarker.com|access-date=20 June 2020}}</ref>  Bender's short and uneventful NBA career marked him as a high-profile draft bust.

===Maccabi Tel Aviv (2020–2021)===
On 23 September 2020, Bender returned to the Israeli team [[Maccabi Tel Aviv]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Bender is back at Maccabi Fox Tel-Aviv |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Euroleague/news/645657/Bender-is-back-at-Maccabi-Fox-Tel-Aviv |website=Eurobasket |access-date=23 September 2020 |date=23 September 2020}}</ref> During the 2020–21 season, he averaged 6.6 points, 3.8 rebounds over 34 EuroLeague games. He suffered a season-ending injury in May 2021 that caused him to miss the entire 2021–22 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dragan Bender on his successful comeback: 'I totally expected this' |url=https://basketnews.com/news-181156-dragan-bender-on-his-successful-comeback-i-totally-expected-this.html |access-date=2022-11-20 |website=basketnews.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Obradoiro (2022)===
On August 23, 2022, Bender signed with [[Obradoiro CAB|Monbus Obradoiro]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/monbus-obradoiro-signs-dragan-bender/|title=Monbus Obradoiro signs Dragan Bender|last=|first=|date=August 23, 2022|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 23, 2022 |last1=Maggi |first1=Alessandro }}</ref> On December 11, he suffered a [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|torn ACL]] injury in his left knee and thus finished a season averaging 17.2 points and 6.6 rebounds on 52.7% shooting from the field in 10 games played for Obradoiro.<ref name="aclinjury-2024update">{{cite news |title=Dragan Bender no reaparecerá esta temporada |url=https://as.com/baloncesto/acb/dragan-bender-no-reaparecera-esta-temporada-n/ |access-date=16 April 2024 |date=2 February 2024 |language=Spanish}}</ref>

==National team career==

===Junior national team===
Bender competed for the Croatian national Under-16 team at the [[2012 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]]. in Latvia and Lithuania. Through five contests, he averaged 2.8 points and 1.4 rebounds in 5.6 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dragan Bender|url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/compID_YUjW-7-FJ,kK9s431Lyr41.season_2012.roundID_8814.playerID_100891.teamID_2168.html|website=FIBAEurope.com|publisher=[[FIBA]]|access-date=6 April 2016}}</ref> The following year, he came back to the [[2013 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]] in Ukraine, improving through 9 games to 9.8 points, 10.8 rebounds and 4.1 assists in 35.4 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dragan Bender|url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/compID_YUjW-7-FJ,kK9s431Lyr41.season_2013.roundID_9441.teamID_2168.playerID_100891.html|website=FIBAEurope.com|publisher=[[FIBA]]|access-date=17 July 2016}}</ref> Bender improved even further, while playing with the Croatian national Under-18 team, at the [[2014 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]] in Turkey. In 9 games, he averaged 14.4 points, 10.4 rebounds and 4.9 assists in 29 minutes per game, helping his team win the bronze medal, and being named to All-Tournament Team in the process.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dragan Bender|url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/compID_8aYeHlfuGF-mF5IqO8aFH1.season_2014.roundID_10067.teamID_2168.playerID_100891.html|website=FIBAEurope.com|publisher=[[FIBA]]|access-date=17 July 2016}}</ref>

In 2015, Bender was selected by Croatia for the [[2015 FIBA Under-19 World Championship|2015 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]] in [[Crete]], Greece, but he was forced to withdraw because the team's players were obliged to wear [[Jordan Brand]] clothes and shoes, due to a sponsorship agreement. Bender had signed a similar agreement with his sponsor [[Adidas]], which prevented him to wear other brands.<ref name="sneakers">{{cite magazine|title=Just for Kicks: Rising star Bender leaves FIBA U19s over sneaker dispute|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2015/07/02/dragan-bender-croatia-nba-fiba-sneakers-adidas-jordan-brand|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=2 July 2015 |access-date=13 March 2016}}</ref> Bender expressed disappointment in the [[Croatian Basketball Federation]]'s decision, even saying they had no reason to attack his loyalty to Croatia, or his family's loyalty to it.<ref>[http://www.myajc.com/news/sports/dragan-bender-top-nba-draft-prospect-talks-about-k/nrjCn/ Dragan Bender, a top NBA draft prospect, talks about Kristaps Porzingis, Croatia and sitcoms]</ref> Adidas later designed a logo-less pair of shoes for Bender, in order for him to play with [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]], since they are also sponsored by Jordan Brand as well, as a response to the Croatian Basketball Federation's stance.<ref>[https://www.si.com/nba/2015/12/10/adidas-dragan-bender-shoe-logo Adidas designs shoe without logo for Croatian PF Dragan Bender]</ref>

===Senior national team===
In June 2017, Bender was granted permission from the [[Phoenix Suns]] to play for the senior [[Croatia men's national basketball team|Croatian national team]] at [[EuroBasket 2017]].<ref>[https://twitter.com/CroSports_/status/880129746784464896 Finally some good news for the Croatian NT...]</ref> At EuroBasket 2017, he averaged 4.3 points, 2 rebounds, and 1 assist per game, in 6 games played.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20171010211850/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/100891/sid/12105/tid/2168/_/2017_FIBA_EuroBasket_Final_Round/index.html Croatia 17 - Dragan Bender.]</ref>

==Player profile==
Bender has been strongly compared to [[Kristaps Porziņģis]] to the point where NBA executives considered him a Top 5 selection similar to Porziņģis because of their playing styles, either due to it being a selling point or being a good cover overall.<ref name=howard>[http://www.nba.com/2016/news/features/scott_howard_cooper/06/17/knicks-porzingis-having-impact-in-this-years-draft/ Bosnian big man getting deep look for top draft position]</ref> However, while Porziņģis may be the stronger shooter and scorer, Bender is consistently labeled as the stronger passer and ball-handler.<ref name="howard"/>

Bender's older brother, Ivan, played college basketball as a forward for the [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland Terrapins]].<ref>[http://www.umterps.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209847610 Ivan Bender Bio]</ref>
